body:
Credit to @yinwu01 for the report (TestLongTurnCopiedFewTimes red once in a full run, 3.2× against a 3× bound, green alone 5 of 5).

**What's wrong**

`TestLongTurnCopiedFewTimes` measures allocations, and its measure reads a neighbor's noise as its own: `allocatedEach` timed its four runs inside **one** `allocated()` window — one `TotalAlloc` reading before, one after — and divided by four. `TotalAlloc` is process-wide, so anything else allocating during that window adds to it, and the division spreads the noise over every run. A ~1.6 MB bump landing in the window reads as +400 KB a run, which is exactly your capture's shape: 6,343,524 against a 5,963,961 bound (3.2×) once under load ~14, and green alone 5 of 5.

**The fix** (test-only; no product file touched)

A few windows of one run each, keeping the **least** (`long_turn_copies_test.go`): noise only ever adds to a window, so the least window is the run's own cost — the same shape the timing measures already settled on. The socket turn-body measure rides the same helper and is otherwise unchanged.

**Verification**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Deterministic injection (1 of 4 runs polluted with 1.6 MB, old structure vs new) | old average 7,157,426 (3.60×) — the pollution/4, exactly; least-of-windows 6,754,624 (3.40×) — the clean cost. The old structure produces your 3.2× shape from the same bump. |
| The real test, current tip `7785c4278`, `-count=10` | ok ×10, read steady at 4,764,0xx (2.40×) — the headroom it was written against |
| Sizing family (`TestRequestBody*`, `TestMarshalSized*`, socket turn body, `-count=2`) | ok |
| Full `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/` | ok, 594.7s, no failures |
| `gofmt -l` on the touched file, `go vet -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/`, `go build ./...` | clean / clean / ok |

From 2f1b7444fb6deb80512de680960b27022a46272d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 02:08:16 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] gateway: the sized-allocation measure takes the least of its
 windows, not one shared window's average (#4882)

allocatedEach measured four runs inside one allocated() window and
divided by four. TotalAlloc is process-wide, so anything else allocating
during that window adds to it, and the division spread the noise over
every run: a 1.6 MB bump landing in the window read as +400 KB a run,
which is how TestLongTurnCopiedFewTimes went red once in a full run
(read 3.2x against a 3x bound) under load ~14, and green alone 5 of 5.

The measure now times a few windows of one run each and keeps the least.
Noise only ever adds to a window, so the least is the run's own cost;
an injected 1.6 MB into one run of four now reads 3.60x on the old
average and 3.40x (the clean cost) on the least, and the real test
stands at its usual 2.40x with the headroom it was written against.

TestLongTurnCopiedFewTimes and the socket turn body measure ride the
same helper and are unchanged otherwise.

-// allocatedEach is what f allocates a run, over a few runs.
+// allocatedEach is what f allocates a run, over a few runs: the least of
+// a few windows of one run each. TotalAlloc is process-wide, so anything
+// else allocating during a window only adds to it; the average of one
+// shared window carried such noise into every run (a 1.6 MB bump read as
+// +400 KB a run, 3.2× against a 3× bound), while the least window is the
+// run's own cost (#4882).
 func allocatedEach(f func()) uint64 {
 	f()
 	const n = 4
-	return allocated(func() {
-		for range n {
-			f()
+	var least uint64
+	for range n {
+		if got := allocated(f); least == 0 || got < least {
+			least = got
 		}
-	}) / n
+	}
+	return least
 }
